name: Gmail
description: Your Gmail in lanes (Unread, Alerts, Read), Grafana alerts grouped, sorted by Jev triage, a thread opened as a clean page to discuss with Claude (a mail reading layout with cc-cockpit 0.13.0+: remote pictures only when you ask, through an optional proxy, the sender's footer folded), Jira mail with its issue (with bronos.jira), mark read / unread. It only ever changes the read state: it never archives, labels, trashes or sends.
author: Oleg Bronzov

remoteImages.title: Remote images
remoteImages.description: Pictures a mail loads from the web tell its sender that you opened it. Ask: they are placeholders, and a bar under the subject offers Show images (this mail) and Always show from the sender (the list below this form). Always: every mail's pictures are loaded when it opens. The plugin fetches them, never the page: no cookies, public addresses only, png, jpeg, gif and webp only.

defaultView.title: Mail opens in
defaultView.description: With cc-cockpit 0.13.0+. Original: the mail as its sender made it (its layout, colours and styles), in a frame that runs no script and loads nothing from the web. Reader: a clean reading layout, where notes go on the text. Each mail has an Original | Reader switch; your last choice for a sender is remembered and wins over this. A mail with no HTML, or one too large to show as made, opens in Reader.

imageProxy.title: Image proxy URL template
imageProxy.description: Optional: fetch remote pictures through your own image proxy, so senders see the proxy instead of you. A URL with {url} where the picture's address goes (encoded), e.g. https://img.example.com/?url={url}. Empty: fetched directly. No public proxy is built in.

clientId.title: OAuth client ID
clientId.description: The client ID of your own Google Cloud OAuth client (a Desktop app client), ending in .apps.googleusercontent.com. Or leave it empty and paste the client file in the Gmail panel: a pasted client wins. Changing it signs you out.

clientSecret.title: OAuth client secret
clientSecret.description: The client secret of the same Desktop app client (Google Cloud console > Google Auth Platform > Clients).

lanes.title: Lanes
lanes.description: Which lanes to show. A hidden lane is not fetched and never sent to triage. Alerts shows only with alert senders. The Inbox plugin sees the unread and read threads of these lanes (unread and read days below) and the alert threads.

read.title: Read (the inbox of the last days)

rowsPerLane.title: Threads per lane
rowsPerLane.description: How many threads a lane shows; the rest are behind Show all at the bottom of the lane.

unreadDays.title: Unread: days back
unreadDays.description: How far back the Unread and Alerts lanes look.

maxUnread.title: Unread: threads fetched
maxUnread.description: The newest unread threads read from Gmail (alerts are listed apart and do not count).

readDays.title: Read: days back
readDays.description: How far back the Read lane looks in the inbox.

maxRead.title: Read: threads fetched
maxRead.description: The newest read inbox threads shown (alerts left out).

alertSenders.title: Alert senders
alertSenders.description: Addresses whose mail goes to the Alerts lane (Grafana alerts are grouped by alert name). Empty: no Alerts lane.

pollMinutes.title: Poll every (minutes)
pollMinutes.description: Only while this project's window is open. A poll first asks Gmail whether anything changed, which costs almost nothing.

alertGroupsInInbox.title: Alerts in the Inbox: one item per alert group
alertGroupsInInbox.description: The Inbox plugin gets an alert group as one item, as the Alerts lane shows it (Mark read marks all its threads read; a new alert brings it back). Off: one item per alert thread.

markReadOnOpen.title: Opening a thread marks it read
markReadOnOpen.description: Opening a thread from the panel marks it read in Gmail, as Gmail does (an alert row: the threads it shows). Off (the default): it stays unread until you press Mark read, so a look does not take it out of Unread.

triageText.title: What triage reads
triageText.description: Full: sender, recipients, subject and the snippets of the thread go to Jev (through Jev triage). Summary: only sender and subject, for employers who object to mail text leaving.

cli.name: gmail
cli.summary: Gmail: status, refresh, list the lanes, show a thread, mark it read or unread, sign in or out, set the OAuth client
cli.usage: gmail status | refresh | list [lane] | show <threadId> | read <threadId> | unread <threadId> | login | logout | client <file.json> | help
